roles.headline: Start fights, hold ground, and turn control into objectives

criteria.label: Initiation and lockdown
criteria.description: Starts or turns fights. Consider target access, reliability, number of targets controlled, and the key spell's downtime.

criteria.label: Frontline and space
criteria.description: Can stand in dangerous space while allies position. Consider damage reduction, sustain, and which enemy damage the hero can take.

criteria.label: Team protection
criteria.description: Uses the hero's kit to save allies, remove disables, or reduce damage reaching the team. Purchased auras are shown in the buy paths.

criteria.label: Wave and objective pressure
criteria.description: Keeps lanes moving and turns an opening into tower or Roshan pressure through wave clear, summons, or objective-enabling abilities.

criteria.label: Impact on low gold
criteria.description: Can still perform a meaningful job through early ability levels and modest items when a major purchase is delayed.

initiation.reason: Berserker's Call forces attacks from enemies in an area. Blink gives him a way to place Call on a cluster.

frontline.reason: Call briefly adds armor and Counter Helix punishes repeated attacks. Long-range magic and damage after Call ends are still threats.

team-protection.reason: Call can peel attackers off an ally when Axe can reach them.

objective-pressure.reason: Counter Helix can help clear waves. In 7.42, attacks that miss Axe still advance its counter.

low-gold.reason: Call can stop enemies who approach him, but starting a reliable fight from outside melee usually needs Blink.

milestoneReasons.bad: Finish Blink after basic boots to bring Call to fights while recovering farm.
milestoneReasons.good: Phase Boots help Axe move and survive before Blink opens stronger Call angles.
milestoneReasons.easy: Keep the Blink timing and spend the extra gold on follow-up and protection.

initiation.reason: Duel holds one target for allied damage. Its limited reach and enemy saves can decide whether the pickoff works.

frontline.reason: Moment of Courage counterattacks provide lifesteal when Legion is allowed to hit. Hard control or burst can interrupt that sustain.

team-protection.reason: Press the Attack applies a strong dispel and helps one ally recover or rejoin the fight.

objective-pressure.reason: Overwhelming Odds helps push a wave, and a successful Duel can create space to take a nearby objective.

low-gold.reason: Press the Attack can contribute early. Starting Duels from fog still depends heavily on a Blink timing and allied follow-up.

milestoneReasons.bad: Buy Blink ahead of Blade Mail when teammates can finish the Duel target.
milestoneReasons.good: Blade Mail comes first on this route when it helps contest the lane. Blink completes your pickoff entry.
milestoneReasons.easy: Blade Mail and Blink establish the Duel timing. Faster farm can add the later upgrade.

initiation.reason: Ravage can stun several nearby enemies. Its long cooldown and dispersed enemy positioning limit the openings.

frontline.reason: Kraken Shell blocks attack damage and cleanses eligible debuffs after enough damage. Anchor Smash weakens nearby enemy attacks.

team-protection.reason: Anchor Smash lowers the attacks of nearby enemies, and Ravage can interrupt a dive on allies.

objective-pressure.reason: Anchor Smash helps clear waves, and Gush lowers enemy armor for physical follow-up. Tidehunter can hold ground near an objective.

low-gold.reason: Kraken Shell and Anchor Smash let him contest close ground on basic items. Ravage can counter-initiate before Blink.

milestoneReasons.bad: Use basic boots to reach Blink sooner and turn an enemy approach into a Ravage.
milestoneReasons.good: Arcane Boots support team mana before Blink expands the angles for Ravage.
milestoneReasons.easy: Blink remains the entry timing. Extra gold can fund the later teamfight items.

initiation.reason: Primal Roar holds a priority target. It still needs cast access and a teammate or controlled unit able to follow up.

frontline.reason: Controlled bodies can occupy space. Beastmaster himself is easier to force back than an offlaner with dedicated damage reduction.

team-protection.reason: Roar and the boar's slow can peel an attacker. Group protection in this guide comes mainly from purchased items.

objective-pressure.reason: Wild Axes manage waves while controlled units and their Inner Beast attack speed help pressure buildings.

low-gold.reason: Roar, boar slows, and Wild Axes all provide jobs before the first expensive item. Extra levels and unit survival still matter.

milestoneReasons.bad: Vladmir's Offering provides a team aura when the first job is to hold or contest an objective.
milestoneReasons.good: Helm of the Dominator brings a controlled creep into the push before Blink. Check which creep ability the team needs.
milestoneReasons.easy: Ristul's Devotion brings group damage and sustain when the team can play together early.
